{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABilUGlw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhL8I4w", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 254, "title": "Add optional CRT display shader presets for composite, S-Video and RGB", "body": "## Problem and motivation

The browser player currently displays the original Rust-rendered framebuffer through a Canvas 2D context (`web/app.js::presentFrame` uses `putImageData`, and `web/index.html` exposes `#screen`). This preserves crisp source pixels but does not reproduce the appearance of a typical 1990s television.

The Sega Saturn was released in Japan on November 22, 1994. It shipped with a stereo AV cable, and composite, S-Video and RGB were relevant analog connection types. The combination of analog video bandwidth and CRT beam/phosphor behavior affects perceived edges, colors, dithering and mesh transparency. A user would like to optionally reproduce that appearance using shaders.

References: [Sega's official Saturn hardware overview](https://www.sega.jp/history/hard/segasaturn/), [original Japanese instruction manual, connection section](https://manuals.plus/m/0dbe18c007e91bcf970f948424e1b9fd202dbd7d7098f48d6e694ffe600151c2.pdf), and [Saturn video output notes](https://consolemods.org/wiki/Saturn:Video_Output_Notes). These establish historical context, not an exact calibrated CRT transfer function.

Inspected baseline: main `55c16f4ea756283abb0d7f62566ee39991c3bc79` (merge of #253). The existing Worker-based video/audio path and ongoing performance work (#138) must be preserved.

## Expected outcome

Add an **optional, lightweight GPU shader post-processing stage** to the browser player's final presentation. Keep the existing unfiltered image as the default and make the effect reversible without restarting the emulator.

Provide one compact, accessible display selector (e.g. "Display filter" in the player controls or Advanced), with these presets:

| Preset | Intended appearance |
| --- | --- |
| Clean (default) | Existing unfiltered, pixelated output, unchanged |
| CRT Composite | Consumer TV style; gentle horizontal luminance softening and chroma bleed, improved blending of dither/mesh patterns, subtle scanline and phosphor response |
| CRT S-Video | Reduced chroma bleed, moderately sharp image, subtle CRT scanline/beam response |
| CRT RGB | Sharpest CRT preset; minimal analog signal blur, subtle scanline/phosphor mask |

These are visually plausible **approximations**, not verified circuit simulations, or claims of identical output from all CRT models. Use restrained defaults that preserve readability and brightness. Avoid exaggerated curvature, noise, flicker, dark stripes, bloom or VHS damage. RF simulation, detailed per-model calibration and complex user-adjustable shader parameters are out of scope.

## Implementation guidance

- Prefer a small original WebGL2 fragment shader (or an equally lightweight supported GPU path), using the existing completed RGBA frame as input and preset uniforms. Aim for a single presentation pass and a bounded sample count; avoid CPU-side full-frame convolution, per-frame GPU resource creation, unnecessary framebuffer copies, blocking GPU readbacks, external shader downloads and new large dependencies.
- Separate the raw emulated framebuffer from its optional presentation. Inspect `web/app.js` (`presentFrame`, `setDisplayRatio`, boot/reset, fullscreen/focus), `web/index.html`, stylesheet, Worker frame acknowledgements and browser tests. An existing 2D canvas cannot also acquire a WebGL context: choose a small, explicit presentation-surface design with a reliable clean/fallback path; preserve the raw/debug readback contract and existing Canvas-based assertions.
- Preserve original dimensions, display aspect policy (including 4:3 for the existing standard output), viewport/fullscreen sizing and device pixel ratio. Define scanlines relative to source video lines, not arbitrary screen pixels. Account for supported low/high resolution and interlaced output; do not blindly apply 240p scanlines to all modes or introduce field flicker/moire. Keep phosphor masks subtle or attenuated when destination resolution is insufficient.
- The filter is purely presentational. It must not modify VDP1/VDP2 output, guest-visible state, CPU/device timing, PCM, input, media, Worker generation or credit semantics. Preserve every-field delivery; do not drop frames or delay emulation intentionally to enable the filter.
- Switching a filter should redraw the last available frame while paused and take effect during play without resetting, advancing guest time, rereading files or losing backup RAM. Preserve existing focus/input and settings-pause semantics.
- Handle unavailable WebGL, shader compilation/link failures, context loss/restoration and resize safely. Fall back to Clean with a concise nonfatal status and allow continued playback; do not turn a display effect failure into a machine error. Keep Clean usable even on devices without GPU acceleration.
- Keep all shader code/assets local and redistributable; if referencing existing shader implementations (e.g. libretro CRT shaders), review licenses and attribution before reuse. Prefer original minimal code. No proprietary BIOS/game data is required.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **UI and presets:** Clean is the default and all three CRT presets are selectable and discoverable. Presets are meaningfully distinct, switch reversibly during playback and while paused, and apply to the display only. Document the intended differences and limitations.
- [ ] **Authentic source preserved:** for the same original guest and deterministic input, raw framebuffer bytes, emulated clocks/state, PCM and input reports are unchanged with every filter and when switching filters. Clean retains the previous pixel output and compatibility path. Existing renderer/Worker and native/Wasm guest assertions remain intact.
- [ ] **Shader verification:** use original, redistributable test patterns (sharp edges, fine text, RGB color bars, alternating/checkerboard dithering, grayscale and flat regions) and actual production-browser GPU rendering. Check bounded, deterministic output at representative scales/resolutions; verify horizontal blending is stronger in Composite than S-Video/RGB, scanline strength is restrained, and solid areas retain reasonable luminance/color. Verify no seams, out-of-bounds sampling or gross clipping. Use appropriate tolerance for GPU rounding; do not rely only on screenshots or subjective approval.
- [ ] **Lifecycle and compatibility:** test resize, DPR, fullscreen, resolution/field changes, paused redraw, boot/reset, Play/Debug, switching modes, context creation/compile failure and context loss/restoration (where supported). Preserve input focus and audio, stale-frame protection, frame acknowledgements and bounded memory. Ensure a fallback still draws correctly without WebGL and that no shader or local firmware/media is fetched/uploaded externally.
- [ ] **Performance:** benchmark the existing normal player versus Clean and each CRT preset using an original guest with real presentation/audio and fixed work, after warmup, in repeat counterbalanced comparisons. Record throughput, p95/p99 presentation gaps, audio shortages/drops and resource/transfer behavior; demonstrate that Clean introduces no meaningful sustained regression beyond measured variation, and keep optional GPU overhead small. Record device/browser/GPU limitations and reduce shader cost if needed. Do not treat 60 Hz callbacks or hidden frame skips as real-time emulation. Authorized local game comparisons are optional.
- [ ] **Regression and documentation:** update README/setup help and a focused validation record, including historical approximation, implementation, source/license and measurements. Use existing test infrastructure, production optimized/compatible Wasm artifacts and pinned Chromium; run applicable native Rust/build/Clippy, fixture checks, Wasm build and all browser groups per development-flow/CI policy. Require successful exact-head PR CI before merge, without weakening hardware, privacy or tested-artifact gates.

## Non-goals

No changes to the emulation core, relaxed/exact scheduler behavior, audio synthesis, internal renderer accuracy, game-specific visual hacks, default forced CRT appearance, large shader framework, or claim of measured physical CRT fidelity. This task does not close #17 or #138.

## Optional validation

A user may compare the presets against their own CRT television or lawful BIOS/game after publication. Physical CRT measurements and subjective aesthetic approval are not mandatory implementation gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All required acceptance checks are executable before merge with original test material.
